summary.headline: Sedemac Q2 FY27 revenue grew over 40% to a record, but EBITDA margin dipped on raw material inflation; H2 EBITDA guided to hold versus H1.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q2 and H1 FY27 revenue, each up more than 40% year on year, with Q2 revenue of roughly Rs 400 crore. EBITDA margin declined on raw material cost inflation, partly offset by operating leverage. Management expects H2 EBITDA to hold at H1 levels despite further PCB cost pressure, with price corrections and the new ISG controller as offsets. The MF3 plant has begun pilot production, and H2 capex is guided lower than H1.

financial_highlights.change: over 40% YoY growth, highest ever quarter

financial_highlights.value: dipped YoY (value not stated in call)
financial_highlights.change: pressured by raw material cost increase, partly offset by operating leverage

financial_highlights.metric: Cumulative capex (plant investments), FY26 to H1 FY27
financial_highlights.change: Rs 333 crore to Rs 450 crore from March to September 2026 per analyst

financial_highlights.value: more than 1 million cumulative; close to 500K in last eight months

segments.name: Mobility - ICE 2/3-wheeler (ISG)
segments.commentary: ISG ECU for export ICE 3-wheelers and domestic/export ICE 3-wheelers fully ramped. ISG on 3 top-10 motorcycle models: two launched and fully ramped, one expected to move to ISG+EFI in FY28.

segments.name: Mobility - Electric 2/3-wheeler (MCU)
segments.commentary: Electric 2-wheeler MCU launched in FY26 and fully ramped; EV revenue share of 2/3-wheeler revenue at about 11.4% in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Industrial (EFI ECUs for home standby generators, North America)
segments.commentary: Demand fell due to a weaker 2025 Atlantic hurricane season; early signs of demand recovery seen in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles (MHCV) - under development
segments.commentary: After-treatment controller, EFI ECUs and MCUs expected in production in the coming few quarters; ACU timing slipped from H2 FY27 to H1 FY28 per analyst question.

segments.name: Power tools - under development
segments.commentary: Motor controller with sensorless control expected in production in H1 FY28; management describes it as early-stage with a large addressable market.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 EBITDA expected to hold versus H1 FY27, with further pressure from PCB cost increases offset by price corrections and the newer-generation ISG controller.
H2 FY27 capex to be lower than H1, as MF3 capex is nearly complete.
Working capital guidance of 13-15% of revenue; currently about 15-16% of annualised Q2 revenue. Management does not expect a substantial change.
Substantial production to shift to MF3 by end of FY27, described as flexible, not a hard timeline.
ISG+EFI shift on one top-10 motorcycle model expected in FY28; European 2/3-wheeler magneto kit business to start production in H1 FY28.
H1 FY27 revenue growth and prospects better than anticipated at the start of the year.
capex_capacity: MF1 is the primary plant and runs at 90% or higher utilisation per the RHP.
MF3 (about 3x the built-up area of MF1) has started pilot production; full transition over the next few quarters. Management expects 65-70% utilisation once fully populated at current revenue.
MF5 land bought at Shoolagiri, Tamil Nadu; plant expected in one to two years and to be substantially bigger than MF3.
Cumulative capex rose by about Rs 120 crore in H1 FY27, mainly MF3 with some MF5 work; Shoolagiri land not included in that increase.
Capex and working capital growth funded through internal accruals and debt, with no equity raise.
demand_pricing: Pricing is negotiated, not cost-plus or pass-through; forex is covered by formula. An ongoing negotiation on price increases is under way given current input inflation.
Management says working capital rise is driven by revenue growth, plus advance purchases to secure supplies amid global uncertainty.
ISG+EFI adoption: OEMs weigh dependence on a single EFI supplier against incumbent global tier-1 relationships; management says the proven-technology concern is largely gone.
Management says ISG on motorcycles has no single inflection point; about 9.5-10 million vehicles adopted ISG in the last 12 months, mainly from Sedemac and Honda.
China: direct sales are difficult; some indirect sales are happening. Direct sales already made to North America industrial customers.
Customer concentration (largest customer minus next four) improved YoY because of new launches and ramp-ups.

qa_highlights.question: How does raw material cost pass-through work for electronics versus metal-indexed auto ancillaries?
qa_highlights.answer: There is no pass-through; pricing is negotiated, with forex adjusted via formula, and an ongoing negotiation on price increases is under way.

qa_highlights.question: Is working capital rising due to supply chain issues, and will it reverse in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital is not up materially as a percentage of revenue (about 15-16% of annualised Q2 revenue) and the rise reflects revenue growth; it does not expect a substantial change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation and capacity plan?
qa_highlights.answer: MF1 runs at 90% or higher utilisation. MF3, about 3x MF1, has begun initial production and would reach 65-70% utilisation if fully populated at current revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why do OEMs choose ISG-only over ISG+EFI?
qa_highlights.answer: The EFI ECU is mandated and traditionally supplied by global tier-1s; OEMs weigh supplier dependence against the proven-technology concern, which management says has largely gone after over 1 million deployments.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the CV after-treatment ECU timeline to shift from H2 FY27 to H1 FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a normal program timeline shift in OEM-supplier relationships and declined to give details.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential volume growth in the last two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up of launches from FY26 plus new launches, as stated on the slide.

risks_watch: Raw material and PCB cost inflation; H2 EBITDA hold depends on price negotiations and the new ISG controller.
Working capital at about 15-16% of revenue, above the 13-15% guidance; inventory around 60 days of sales; short-term borrowings up about Rs 110 crore in H1.
MF3 transition timing (flexible, not hard) and the MF5 build; ROCE dip while new plants are not yet operational.
Timeline slippage in CV programs (ACU shifted to H1 FY28); power tool market still at early engagement stage with no assured outcome.
Industrial EFI demand tied to North American hurricane season; recovery signs only early.
Management declined to share capex split, ISG+EFI share, or forward volumes, limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on revenue and product ramp-ups, but guarded on margins, timelines and forward metrics, with management repeatedly declining to give numbers on pipeline, ISG+EFI mix, and power tool outcomes.
key_quotes: So overall, we expect our EBITDA to hold for H2 as compared to H1FY27.
There is no pass-through. It is negotiated broadly and secondly, our pricing is quite different from typical auto ancillary, where it's cost plus.

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 EBITDA to hold versus H1 and H1 revenue growth above 40%, backed by MF3 pilot production (MF1 at ~90% utilisation, MF3 targeted at 65-70%) and new ISG/EFI programmes, with MF5 at Shoolagiri in 1-2 years, though no explicit revenue growth figure for FY27 was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA guided to hold vs H1 FY27 (no expansion), with PCB cost increases offset only by price corrections and the new ISG controller; margin already dipped YoY on raw material inflation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: MF3 (about 3x MF1 built-up area) has started pilot production with substantial production to shift by end of FY27; MF1 runs at 90%+ utilisation and MF3 targets 65-70% once fully populated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 FY27 revenue up over 40% YoY to roughly Rs 400 crore and TTM ECUs sold up 44% to about 4.6 million, backed by ISG ramp-ups and new launches; ISG+EFI shipments near 500K in last eight months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: MF1 at 90%+ utilisation and MF5 at Shoolagiri (land bought, plant in 1-2 years, substantially bigger than MF3) already committed; cumulative capex rose to Rs 450 crore, though H2 FY27 capex is guided lower than H1.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue growth above 40% was better than anticipated at the start of the year, but management guided only to H2 EBITDA holding and gave no explicit FY27 growth figure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Further PCB cost inflation could pressure H2 EBITDA; hold depends on price negotiations still ongoing, and working capital at 15-16% of revenue is above the 13-15% guidance (though management does not expect a substantial change).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: European 2/3-wheeler magneto kit production to start H1 FY28, one top-10 motorcycle model moves to ISG+EFI in FY28, and CV after-treatment ECU/EFI ECU/MCU expected in production over coming quarters (ACU slipped to H1 FY28).

rows.label: Price negotiations to offset PCB and raw material inflation
rows.why: Pricing is negotiated with no pass-through; an ongoing negotiation on price increases is under way, and H2 EBITDA hold relies on price corrections and the new ISG controller.

rows.label: North America industrial EFI demand recovery
rows.why: Demand for home standby generator EFI ECUs fell on a weaker 2025 hurricane season, with only early signs of recovery in H1 FY27.

rows.label: Power tool motor controller in production
rows.why: Sensorless motor controller expected in production in H1 FY28, but management calls it early-stage with no assured outcome.
